text:
alex: quick heads-up — our longctx canary shows steady KV memory growth over 36h, looks correlated with session-sticky keys :eyes:

maria: logs or profile dump?

alex: grabbing pprof now, but initial heap allocs point to many small page fragments from kv_store.cpp

alex: snippet from cache key gen: `fmt::format("{}/{}:{}", tenant, model, hash(prefix)+session_hint)` — session_hint is `user_id` for the canary

jin: that user_id sticky hint is high-cardinality, unsurprising it fragments. are we including tenant salts anywhere?

alex: tenant salt present but constant per-tenant. curious part: eviction activity spikes whenever a popular prefix gets mixed with lots of distinct session_hints — pages get churned instead of reused

sam: observed similar on staging when we had sticky sessions turned on. effect: less cross-request reuse -> more memory churn and paging. what did the canary's eviction rate look like? numbers?

maria: from the eviction trace: `evict_ops/s` jumped from ~12 to ~180 during peak, live pages rose from 42k -> 91k, swap-outs increased 6x. TTL smoothing didn't help.

alex: i toggled sticky=false for that tenant 2h ago (quick kill switch) — mem usage flattened and eviction ops dropped by ~4x. suggests the session_hint is the culprit.

jin: option: change cache key shape to tiered keying — `tenant:model:prefix_hash` primary, then optional `|session_bucket` for sticky. session_bucket = hash(user_id) % B where B is small (e.g., 16). reduces cardinality but keeps some stickiness.

sam: agree. naive bucketing reduces fragmentation but risks cross-tenant collision? we already have tenant prefix so ok. need deterministic bucket count per tenant to avoid changing buckets during rollouts.

maria: also consider prefix-length gating: for prefixes > 8k tokens, disable session_bucket entirely and use pure prefix key — longctx flows benefit most from cross-request reuse.

alex: i'm +1 for both: small bucketed stickiness + prefix-length gating. low risk and incremental. can we add telemetry to measure reuse hit-rate by (prefix_len, bucket_id) to validate?

jin: i'll draft a patch — will include metrics: reuse_hits, reuse_misses, eviction_rate, live_pages by bucket. also add an opt-in header `X-KV-sticky: bucketed` for canary control.

sam: rollout plan: 1) canary single tenant with B=8 and prefix gating, 2) monitor for 24h, 3) expand to cohort tenants. if hit-rate improves and eviction drops, increase B to 16 for select tenants.

ops-bot: deploy started to canary (tenant: redwood-canary-3) — image: kv-reuse-buckets:v2026.03.18 — watch traces and alert on eviction_rate>50/s for 10m.

maria: noted. i'll hook the eviction_rate alert and add dashboards for bucket reuse.

alex: thanks all — this should reduce longctx memory growth without losing sticky perf for small prefixes. will follow up with pprof output once the canary completes. :thumbsup:
